1.1.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is the South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in South Ogan Komering Ulu. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time which, in interacting with the environment and community attitudes, may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government commitments and resources, the community and the business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not adequately met, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Woman victim of violence is a Woman who experiences actions that result in suffering or distress physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victim of violence is a Child who experiences actions that result in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender-sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and meet the needs of the victim. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence in accordance with established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for coaching and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Article 7

(1) The Kabupaten Government in efforts to protect Women is obligated and responsible to: a. guarantee Women's Rights without discrimination in accordance with the provisions of Legislation; b. establish and implement policy programs and activities for the protection of Women; c. cooperate with the community and/or Community Organizations in the implementation of Women's Protection in accordance with the provisions of Legislation;

d. carry out rehabilitation and empowerment of Women who are victims of violence; e. provide special protection to Women victims of violence and human trafficking; and

f. take preventive action in order to prevent violations of Women's rights.

(2) The responsibility of the Kabupaten Government in efforts to protect Women's Rights as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by DPPKBP-PPPA.

Article 47

(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence. (2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1)

aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence requiring safe houses include:

a. life threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services shall be regulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 43

(1) Complaints of acts of violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 42 may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. Victims;
b. Family;
c. Community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of Women and Children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 42 are authorized to handle Women and Children victims of violence obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 10

(1) The community is obliged and responsible in administering the protection of Women and Children including:

a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. monitoring the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children. (2) Community responsibility as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Part One

Handling of Women and Children Victims of Violence Article 40

The implementation of handling Women and Children victims of violence includes:

a. handling of complaints from victims of violence; b. health services;
c. social rehabilitation;
d. law enforcement and legal aid; and
e. repatriation and social reintegration.

Part Five

Repatriation Services and Social Reintegration Article 51

(1) Repatriation of victims of violence is aimed at returning Women and Children victims of violence to their area of origin.

(2) Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

(3) The Regency Government carries out repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 49

(1) Law enforcement services and legal assistance are actions of law enforcement officials provided to Women and Children victims of violence and/or witnesses.

(2) Law enforcement services and legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is the South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in South Ogan Komering Ulu. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time which, in interacting with the environment and community attitudes, may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government commitments and resources, the community and the business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not adequately met, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Woman victim of violence is a Woman who experiences actions that result in suffering or distress physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victim of violence is a Child who experiences actions that result in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender-sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and meet the needs of the victim. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence in accordance with established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for coaching and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

(1) The Kabupaten Government in efforts to protect Women is obligated and responsible to: a. guarantee Women's Rights without discrimination in accordance with the provisions of Legislation; b. establish and implement policy programs and activities for the protection of Women; c. cooperate with the community and/or Community Organizations in the implementation of Women's Protection in accordance with the provisions of Legislation;

d. carry out rehabilitation and empowerment of Women who are victims of violence; e. provide special protection to Women victims of violence and human trafficking; and

f. take preventive action in order to prevent violations of Women's rights.

(2) The responsibility of the Kabupaten Government in efforts to protect Women's Rights as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by DPPKBP-PPPA.

Article 10

(1) The community is obliged and responsible in administering the protection of Women and Children including:

a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. monitoring the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children. (2) Community responsibility as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 14

(1) Efforts made by the community to prevent violations of Women's rights include:

a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may cause violations of Women's rights;
b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and family environment; and
c. preventing unregistered marriage/siri marriage.
(2) Efforts made to prevent violations of Children's rights include: a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that cause violations of Children's rights;
b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and family environment; and
c. preventing marriage at Child age.

Article 28

(1) The Regency Government provides scholarships and/or educational assistance for:

a. children from poor families;
b. neglected children; and
c. children residing in remote areas. (2) The implementation of scholarship programs and/or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by the participation of the community and community organizations.
(3) Further provisions regarding the provision of scholarships and or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 47

(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence. (2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1)

aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence requiring safe houses include:

a. life threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services shall be regulated by Regional Regulation.

(1) The Regency Government is obliged to provide care for neglected Children.

Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. (1) Employers who employ Women are required to maintain decency, safety and security in the workplace.

(2) Employers are required to place Women workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.

Article 20

(1) Women workers/laborers who are at most 18 (eighteen) years old are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB and 07.00 WIB.

(2) Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant Women workers/laborers who, according to a doctor's statement, are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB to 07.00 WIB.

(3) Employers who employ Women workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB and 07.00 WIB, are required to:

a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and b. maintain decency and security in the workplace.
(4) Employers are required to provide shuttle transportation for Women workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB and 05.00 WIB.

Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender-sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and meet the needs of the victim. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence in accordance with established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for coaching and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Article 47

(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence. (2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1)

aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.

aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services shall be regulated by Regional Regulation.

Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender-sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and meet the needs of the victim. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence in accordance with established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for coaching and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

(1) The Kabupaten Government in efforts to protect Women is obligated and responsible to: a. guarantee Women's Rights without discrimination in accordance with the provisions of Legislation; b. establish and implement policy programs and activities for the protection of Women; c. cooperate with the community and/or Community Organizations in the implementation of Women's Protection in accordance with the provisions of Legislation;

d. carry out rehabilitation and empowerment of Women who are victims of violence; e. provide special protection to Women victims of violence and human trafficking; and

f. take preventive action in order to prevent violations of Women's rights.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is the South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in South Ogan Komering Ulu. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time which, in interacting with the environment and community attitudes, may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government commitments and resources, the community and the business world that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not adequately met, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Woman victim of violence is a Woman who experiences actions that result in suffering or distress physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victim of violence is a Child who experiences actions that result in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the State or between States, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officers authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender-sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and meet the needs of the victim. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence in accordance with established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for coaching and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not engage in activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.
